results.conclusion: Recovery is part of that liquidity story. CancelAfter permits cancellation after the validated ledger deadline; it does not automatically return funds. Policy must submit EscrowCancel and confirm successful validation before describing principal as returned. Fees remain spent. A refund after completed key publication is a different writer-signed Payment and requires writer cooperation. Throughout provisioning, purchase and recovery, the budget remains the spending authority and durable intent identity prevents duplicate principal purchases. These observations support bounded mechanism claims only. Asset provisioning and buying research are separate operations. The builder feedback records dated Testnet observations rather than a current mainnet survey. That distinction is essential for stablecoins: a successful direct token payment does not prove that the same issuer permits token escrow. A wallet balance does not establish that an agent may spend it, and a price displayed in SGD is not an independently measured foreign exchange rate. The basic purchase contract requires an expected network, asset and issuer before policy signs. XRP uses integer drops, with one million drops per XRP. An issued asset also needs the currency and issuer identity; the currency name alone is insufficient. The buyer checks destination, exact amount, invoice binding, expiry and policy limits. Validated settlement must show successful delivery. The requested Amount alone does not prove what arrived, particularly for partial payments. These are payment validation requirements, not decisions delegated to the language model. Token escrow adds issuer requirements beyond holding an issued balance. The builder feedback's 7 November entry B26 records an earlier validated observation: TokenEscrow was enabled, but the official RLUSD Testnet issuer flags lacked AllowTrustLineLocking. The documented implication was that official RLUSD escrow was blocked by issuer permission. The record distinguishes that code-derived blocker from an actually submitted rejection transaction. A trust line does not supply missing issuer consent. Recheck the issuer and network before claiming present support; this article itself performs no fresh ledger query. The available workaround is explicit about substitution. XRP remains the default key-reveal asset, while TEST-SGD is a labelled issued-token stand-in for experiments. TEST-SGD is not official RLUSD and does not demonstrate RLUSD issuer cooperation. Direct RLUSD Testnet payments and conditional token escrow are separate evidence classes. A report should identify which it tested, with the exact transaction hash and issuer, rather than describing every successful token transaction as proof of the same settlement mode. Nothing here is redeemable money or a production stablecoin guarantee. Funding observations also need labels. The 3 November builder feedback records public RLUSD faucet authentication friction and historical bounded native Testnet DEX provisioning. In those samples, acquisition cost about 25.1 Testnet XRP for two RLUSD. That arbitrary test exchange rate is not economic evidence. The workaround used an exact self-payment, a bounded SendMax and a fee cap, checked validated delivered_amount, and kept provisioning separate from product purchases. It does not establish an automatic exchange strategy for the research agent or an available mainnet funding route. A DEX provisioning observation likewise does not establish AMM behavior. The cited repository evidence concerns acquiring a test balance, not measuring pool pricing, liquidity provision or agent routing through an AMM. No AMM performance result is claimed here. When evaluating agent payments, ask which asset was already provisioned, which exact asset policy authorized, and whether conversion happened outside the purchase loop. Do not infer a pool mechanism from an exchange label. This boundary prevents a setup workaround from becoming an unsupported product capability claim. Fees and reserves constrain even faucet-funded micropayments. Builder feedback B19 records 12-drop create and cancel fees and a 423-drop conditional finish using xrpl.js 4.7.0. Its observed OwnerCount changed from zero to one and back to zero with a 0.2 XRP increment. These are dated measurements, not universal fee quotes. A wallet needs terminal transaction fee headroom and object reserve liquidity as well as purchase principal. The number of concurrent escrow objects can therefore constrain capacity independently of article prices or burned network fees.

results.conclusion: EscrowCreate has no InvoiceID. Its only memo uses MemoType = HEX("researchagent/escrow-v1") and MemoData = HEX(UTF8(canonical signed terms)). The facilitator validates the whole memo, signature, account, amount, destination, condition, deadline, LastLedgerSequence and fee. /facilitator/verify checks binding; /facilitator/settle and paid GET confirm the validated create and object, then journal a conditional exact-version grant. Response success: false, escrowState: "LOCKED" explicitly distinguishes locked funds from settlement. Only the private proof worker receives these bytes. A passed proof alone never makes them accessible: a validated finish is also required. Direct-payment challenge/refund logic does not apply to escrow cancellation. Buyer SQLite stores a separate escrow row and (intent, operation) outbox, with UNIQUE intent/invoice, transaction hash and (owner, create Sequence). The existing direct-payment submissions table is untouched. All three operations share the payer queue. A restart looks up and resubmits the same create; no timeout authorizes another principal. Expired/failed terminal signatures may be archived and replaced only after ledger proof, referencing the same object. An unresolved escaped finish is reconciled before cancellation. A Stop cannot undo a submitted finish. If a revealed fulfillment is relayed by another account, recovery checks the validated object and paginated account history, then confirms the winning terminal hash. Missing object/history alone never means refunded. The live reconciler cancels due objects without writer connectivity; expiry itself does not return funds. The x402 headers are PAYMENT-REQUIRED, which carries the challenge; PAYMENT-SIGNATURE carries the buyer payment proof; PAYMENT-RESPONSE carries settlement information. The x402 buyer first requests a resource and receives payment requirements rather than premium content. The exact resource, version, seller wallet, network and amount must remain bound throughout negotiation. A model can assess usefulness but cannot initiate payment. Deterministic policy checks the authorized budget and reserves exposure before signing or submitting a purchase. Every writer is a facilitator: the publisher host serves /w/:slug/..., and the buyer pays the writer's own wallet on XRPL Testnet (xrpl:1, scheme exact, asset XRP in integer drops). Code: publisher/routes.ts, publisher/facilitator.ts, publisher/challenge.ts, shared/x402.ts, server/purchases.ts. Some XRPL and older x402 examples use different headers. Do not combine them from memory. Pin the facilitator and SDK versions, capture the actual challenge and retry exchange in an integration test, and record the version in the technical receipt. Relevant CAIP-2 network identifiers are xrpl:0 for Mainnet, xrpl:1 for Testnet, and xrpl:2 for Devnet. The first live proof should use XRP on Testnet. One XRP equals one million drops; quote amounts must use exact integer drop strings. LOCKED principal stays reservedMinor; only RELEASED becomes spent. A CANCELLED receipt records zero spent principal and the cancel hash, rather than inventing a refund Payment. Cancelled authority cannot be reused inside the run or wallet day. Public API/SDK intents and receipts carry escrow.state, owner, create Sequence, deadline, transaction hashes and proofOk; no secret or blob. src/ is unchanged. The balance check includes live base + OwnerCount reserve, one extra owner increment (currently 0.2 XRP), principal and create/terminal fee headroom. After creation, refreshed validated balance already excludes principal; it is not deducted twice.
